feature: Trajectory tier: deterministic tool-call checks in session_judge.py
problem: Only 3 scenarios use trajectory_quality, all routed to LLM judge. No deterministic trajectory scoring exists. Industry standard (trajscore, trajectly, AgentEvals) is to check tool-call loops, read-before-write, step efficiency, and skeleton matching deterministically.
proposed_solution: New trajectory tier between structural and LLM with 7 deterministic checks in tests/eval/trajectory_checks.py. Sessions without trace (_has_trace false) return []. trajectory_skeleton optional YAML field for per-scenario subsequence matching.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: judge_session(..., tiers={'trajectory'}) produces results with tier: 'trajectory'
AC2: CLI --tier trajectory runs only trajectory checks; --tier choices include 'trajectory'
AC3: Session where _has_trace() is False → check_trajectory() returns []; judge_session summary (total, pass, fail) is identical with and without trajectory in tiers set
AC4: Synthetic trace with 3 consecutive identical (name, args_hash) tool calls → FAIL (threshold: >2 consecutive)
AC5: Step efficiency uses difficulty ranges: easy 5-25, medium 10-50, hard 20-100. Missing difficulty defaults to medium. 30 calls on easy → FAIL; 15 on easy → PASS
AC6: Write to foo.py without prior Read of foo.py → FAIL; Read then Write → PASS. Write and StrReplace both count as write tools

AC7: Scenario with trajectory_skeleton [{tool: Read, path_contains: state.json}] and trace containing that Read → PASS; missing → FAIL. No trajectory_skeleton → skeleton criterion omitted entirely. Schema: {tool, path_contains?, command_contains?, after?}
AC8: 4 edits with 3 StrReplace on same file → FAIL (>50%); 2 edits, 1 same-file StrReplace → PASS. total_edits == 0 → PASS
AC9: 4 consecutive assistant response steps without any tool call → FAIL (threshold: >3 consecutive idle steps)

AC10: Shell exit_code != 0 followed by 3 steps with no corrective action → FAIL. Corrective = Read/Write/StrReplace/Shell with different command on related path. Same failing command repeated does not count as recovery
AC11: session_report classify_dimension({'tier': 'trajectory'}) returns 'trajectory'; DIMENSIONS includes 'trajectory'; table column renders
AC12: All 28 scenario YAMLs load without error; make validate passes

AC13: 7 fixed criterion strings stable across runs: 'No repeated identical tool calls', 'Tool call count within difficulty range', 'Read before write on same file', 'Trajectory skeleton satisfied', 'Edit backtracking ratio acceptable', 'No excessive idle turns without tools', 'Shell errors followed by recovery within 3 steps'
AC14: Trajectory tier emits only PASS or FAIL verdicts — never UNCERTAIN, UNMATCHED, or SKIP
AC15: When --tier is omitted and _has_trace() is true, tiers_run includes 'trajectory'. Default tier set: {computational, structural, trajectory} (+ llm when API key present)
edge_cases: EC1: total_edits == 0 → backtracking PASS (covered by AC8)
EC2: Shell toolCall (not shellConversationTurn) with non-zero exit parsed from result text → error recovery detects it
EC3: trajectory_skeleton with after: constraint where steps are out of order → FAIL
EC4: Mixed tier run with trajectory + llm: LLM trajectory_quality criteria still run for the 3 planning scenarios; total result count >= prior LLM-only count
EC5: Args equality for loops uses canonical JSON (sorted keys) hash
EC6: Transcript with turns but zero toolCalls in conversation → same as no trace (return [])
verification_method: 1. python -c 'import tests.eval.trajectory_checks' 2. python -m pytest tests/eval/test_session_judge_trajectory.py -q (>=1 test per check + orchestration) 3. make validate 4. Each AC maps to named test: test_ac1_tier_in_results through test_ac15_default_tiers
